#5220. Why This Analyst Isn’t Rushing to Buy XRP Below $1 Despite Predicting an Explosive Rally to $10

XRP’s return below the psychologically important $1 level hasn’t convinced every investor that it is time to buy the dip. Despite believing the payments-based token could eventually climb to a staggering $10, one trader is holding back. His cautious stance raises an interesting question: if XRP has such massive upside potential, why is he waiting on the sidelines?

In a November 19 post on X, crypto trader VirtualBacon identified the $1 price level as a potential bottoming zone for XRP in the current market cycle. The analyst suggested that the cryptocurrency may be approaching the lower end of its correction, even as selling pressure continues to weigh on its price.

“For me, $1 is roughly the bottom area for this cycle,” he stated.

While he described the $1 mark as the approximate bottoming zone for XRP during the ongoing cycle, he did not suggest that a definitive price floor had already been established.

His hesitation stems from the belief that investors will still have plenty of opportunities to accumulate alternative cryptocurrencies even after the broader market begins recovering. In his view, many altcoins could remain relatively cheap early in the next market rebound, meaning investors don’t necessarily need to rush into XRP before its downtrend runs its course.

“I’m not buying it yet,” he explained, making it clear that he would rather wait for a more favorable entry point than rush into the market.

XRP was trading at $0.9647 at the time of publication, down 2.3% over the previous 24 hours. The latest pullback followed a brief recovery to $1 on November 18, 2026, which proved short-lived as investors took profits, pushing the token back below the key psychological threshold.

Although VirtualBacon is not ready to accumulate XRP at current prices, he remains optimistic about its longer-term potential. The pundit believes the cryptocurrency could eventually reach $10, although he sees limited room for significant gains beyond that valuation.

A rally to $10 would represent a major milestone for XRP, pushing its market capitalization to approximately $635 billion based on a circulating supply of 63.52 billion tokens. This would place the cryptocurrency among the largest digital assets by market value and require its valuation to grow more than tenfold from current levels.

The projected price target also highlights the scale of growth XRP would need. At $10 per token, its fully diluted valuation, calculated using the maximum supply of 100 billion XRP, would reach approximately $1 trillion.

However, reaching such a valuation would require sustained demand, increased market participation, and significant capital flowing into the cryptocurrency. Notably, while VirtualBacon considers $10 achievable over the longer term, his outlook suggests that he sees this level as a more realistic upper target rather than expecting XRP to deliver substantially higher gains.

"Rich Dad Poor Dad" author Robert Kiyosaki wrote on X on Nov. 20 that he is "most excited about Bitcoin's crash" and is "waiting to buy more." On the same day, Bitcoin was trading at $61,666, more than 50% below its October 2025 peak of about $126,000.

Gold fell 1.24% to $3,579 an ounce, and silver lost 0.95% to $42.42, according to TradingView data. The S&P 500 dropped 2.02% on the same day.

Kiyosaki started his post with a question. "CRASH: Good or Bad? Gold, silver, Bitcoin, crashing. Weak hands selling. Strong hands waiting to buy?" he wrote.

According to Kiyosaki, the reasons include "incompetence in FED, Banks, and Bond markets." He also wrote that America's debt is "only to grow bigger" as "Banksters steal our wealth via their system legally."

The author pointed to Bitcoin's fixed supply. There will be only 21 million BTC in total, and about 20 million coins have already been mined, Kiyosaki wrote. "As far as I know, there has never been a 'money' such as Bitcoin ever before," he added.

"With price of Bitcoin crashing, I can't wait to buy more coins… just because only 21 million are ever to be mined. It could be a 'nothing burger'…. or the best money I've ever spent," Kiyosaki wrote.

In late August, Kiyosaki said on podcasts that he owed creditors $1.2 billion. His ex-wife and business partner, Kim Kiyosaki, later said that the figure covered the loans of a partnership that owns about 1,500 rental units. "We have a lot of apartment houses with our partners," she said.

According to Kim Kiyosaki, Robert Kiyosaki's own share of the debt is $30 million to $60 million. Each of their real estate investments is held in a separate LLC. Robert Kiyosaki also commented on the debt at the time. "If it all comes to hell, you can talk to my attorney," he said.

In 2012, Kiyosaki's company Rich Global LLC filed for bankruptcy after a court ordered it to pay about $24 million.

#5218. Anthropic IPO Price Could Top $80 And Pre-IPO Traders Are Copying the SpaceX Script: What Traders Should Expect

The Anthropic IPO may price above $80. Hyperliquid’s pre-IPO contract sits 24% higher, the setup SpaceX had before it listed.

The Anthropic IPO could price above $80 a share on Wednesday evening, above the $70 to $78 range the Claude AI maker set last week, The Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday. The newspaper cited stronger-than-expected investor demand. Its advisers have discussed a valuation of $1.5 trillion to $1.6 trillion.

The shares are due to start trading on Nasdaq on Thursday, November 19, under the ticker ANT.

⚠️ What if $ANT mirrors $SPCX after the IPO? pic.twitter.com/pMd9aC7KQb

— Rand Group (@randgroup) November 18, 2026

Crypto traders have been betting on the Anthropic IPO for weeks. On Hyperliquid, a pre-IPO contract that tracks one ANT share trades near $99, about 23% above $80.

We have seen this setup before. The night before SpaceX listed in June, the same kind of contract traded 28% above its $135 IPO price. SpaceX then closed its first day 19% up, below what the contract had promised.

So what should traders know before the bell rings on Thursday?

Anthropic launched its roadshow, the week when a company pitches its shares to large investors, on November 10. Its announcement set the terms:

Demand has run ahead of that. Pricing above $80 would lift the valuation toward the $1.5 trillion to $1.6 trillion the advisers discussed. The final price is set after the US market closes on Wednesday, and the shares open on Thursday.

That price is what large investors pay in the Anthropic IPO. Most retail traders will buy at the opening price instead, which can be far higher.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

Hyperliquid, a crypto exchange, lists contracts that let traders bet on a company’s share price before it lists. We compared its Anthropic contract with the one it ran for SpaceX, counting back from each listing day.

The SpaceX contract was right that the shares would jump, but too optimistic about how far. If Anthropic followed the same pattern, a 7% gap from Wednesday’s contract price would put ANT’s first close in the low $90s. That is a pattern from one listing, not a forecast.

EXPLORE: Bitcoin Price Tumbles 19% Ahead of Anthropic IPO: Is SpaceX Crash Repeating?

On the hourly chart, Hyperliquid’s ANT contract trades at $98.83, down from $138 when it started trading on October 26.

The number to watch before the Anthropic IPO opens is tonight’s final price. Every dollar above $80 shrinks the contract’s 24% premium, and with it the room for the first-day pop that pre-IPO traders are betting on.

#5214. BlackRock Records Largest Bitcoin Outflow in History

BlackRock, the leading asset management firm and Bitcoin’s largest ETF issuer, sparked discussions earlier today following a massive Bitcoin sale by the company.

The latest data showcased by SosoValue shows that the leading Bitcoin fund has witnessed massive single-day withdrawals from investors who have ventured into its Bitcoin investment product.

Earlier today, BlackRock sold over half a billion dollars’ worth of Bitcoin after its spot Bitcoin ETF, also known as iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), recorded a total of $541.08 million in net outflows.

This massive outflow has come as Bitcoin’s price decline continues to intensify, causing investors to aggressively pull their money out of the fund amid growing market fear.

While this marks the third time this week that BlackRock has recorded a net outflow amid persistent market volatility, it also marks the largest single-day outflow BlackRock has recorded since its launch.

Apparently, the record-breaking withdrawal that the fund just witnessed suggests that institutional and traditional investors are becoming less willing to retain their exposure to Bitcoin through asset managers, especially as Bitcoin’s price continues to slump further.

Although BlackRock has just suffered the largest withdrawal since it launched its Bitcoin investment product, the record outflow did not alter its dominance in the market.

Further data shows that the BlackRock spot Bitcoin ETF still boasts a massive $47.82 billion in assets under management, spotlighting its leadership in the Bitcoin ETF market.

This positions it far ahead of Fidelity, which ranks as the second-largest Bitcoin ETF with just $10.62 billion in net assets.

Bitcoin rebounds from $55,326 to above $60,000, recovering more than 8% after hitting its lowest level since September 2024.

Ethereum, Solana, XRP and BNB also recover, as buyers return following a sharp liquidation-driven sell-off.

The rebound faces a major test, with ETF outflows, weak risk appetite and broader market volatility continuing to pressure cryptocurrencies.

The crypto market today is staging a sharp recovery after Bitcoin plunged to a two-year low, triggering aggressive selling across digital assets. Bitcoin price rebounded more than 8% from its intraday low of $55,326 and briefly reclaimed $60,000, while major altcoins also recovered. The bounce followed a brutal sell-off that pushed Bitcoin below key support levels and intensified fears of a deeper market downturn.

However, the recovery comes against a backdrop of weakening institutional demand, heavy ETF withdrawals and a broader retreat from risk assets, leaving investors questioning whether the latest rally marks a genuine reversal or simply a temporary rebound.

Bitcoin price recovered sharply after falling to $55,326, its lowest level since September 2024. The cryptocurrency subsequently bounced above $60,000, recovering a significant portion of its intraday losses as buyers stepped in following the steep decline.

The sell-off had pushed BTC below its previous bear-market low near $57,742, breaking a level that had held since September 2024. Bitcoin has also lost more than half its value from its record high near $126,200 reached in October 2025, highlighting the scale of the correction.

The rebound has offered short-term relief, but Bitcoin remains vulnerable after a weekly decline and a broader deterioration in market sentiment.

The recovery extended across major cryptocurrencies, although the rebound followed substantial losses earlier in the session. The broad-based recovery suggests traders are attempting to buy into the sell-off after prices fell sharply.

However, the earlier decline remained significant, with Ethereum price still below $1800, and XRP below $1, while Solana is still below $100 and other major tokens still facing pressure from the broader market downturn.

The rebound appears to have been driven by dip-buying after an aggressive sell-off, with easing liquidation pressure allowing prices to recover. Bitcoin’s decline below key support levels triggered forced selling among leveraged traders. As prices approached the $55,000 region, the sharp decline created an opportunity for traders to buy at lower levels, helping BTC recover rapidly.

But the broader market’s underlying conditions remain fragile. Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies have faced pressure from weakening technology stocks, concerns over AI valuations, higher borrowing costs and institutional withdrawals from spot Bitcoin ETFs.

US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $582 million in net outflows, while monthly withdrawals have approached $3.5 billion, weakening a major source of institutional demand. The combination of ETF redemptions and broader risk aversion has left the market susceptible to sharp price swings.

Bitcoin’s recovery above $60,000 is an important short-term development, but it does not yet establish that the market has bottomed. The cryptocurrency needs to hold above reclaimed levels and regain additional resistance zones to strengthen the bullish case. A renewed breakdown could quickly erase the rebound, particularly if institutional outflows continue or broader markets remain under pressure.

The crypto market today is witnessing a sharp relief rally, but Bitcoin’s ability to sustain its recovery above $60,000 will determine whether buyers can turn the bounce into a broader reversal or whether the market faces another wave of selling.

Three XRP Ledger amendments linked to native lending have each gained two validator votes since Nov. 17, according to XRPScan data. As of Nov. 20, 2026, Single Asset Vault (XLS-65) had 25 votes, and Lending Protocol (XLS-66) and the LendingProtocolV1_1 patch had 24 votes each.

XRPScan data shows that LendingProtocolV1_1 has been up for a vote since Sept. 29, 2026, when it came with the v3.4.0 release. According to the patch's voting history, it had about 19 votes for most of October. It started to gain votes again in late October. XRP was trading at $0.96 on Friday.

Lending is built directly into the XRP Ledger's code, with no third-party smart contracts. According to Ripple, lenders deposit into a Single Asset Vault, and the Lending Protocol lets loan brokers use that capital "to issue loans and track repayments onchain."

The model is close to how banks lend. Loans have fixed terms and a repayment schedule, and credit brokers vet borrowers before the loans are issued. On Nov. 19, Clearpool showed the full lending flow on the XRPL Devnet with Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin. In the demo, "An approved lender funds a private vault, and a borrower accepts and repays a loan underwritten offchain by a broker," Clearpool wrote.

Through Single Asset Vault (XLS-65), XRP holders will be able to deposit their coins into shared liquidity pools, and institutional borrowers will take loans from those pools at a fixed rate. After the loan is repaid, "the lender redeems at a higher share price," according to the Clearpool demo.

The amendments still need more votes before they can activate. "An amendment needs more than 80% support, held for 14 days, to activate," XRPScan says on its amendment pages. For the current set of 35 validators, the site puts the threshold at "more than 80% of 35 votes, so 29 needed."

#5210. Bitcoin Bounces From $62K: Is Gold and Silver’s 14% Crash Sending Money Into Crypto?

BTC bounced from $62K as silver fell 14% since Nov 9. What does fund trading reveal, and is there really a shift from metals into Bitcoin?

In today’s Bitcoin news, on November 19, silver and gold are extending their sell-off, but Bitcoin is holding its ground near $63,800. BTC has bounced off the $62,000 level for the second time in four days, raising the question of whether crypto’s sell-off is finally losing steam and investors are starting to move money back into digital assets.

Silver futures closed Wednesday at $45 an ounce, down 4.8% on the day and 14% since November 9, while gold fell another 3.2%.

JUST IN: $1,400,000,000,000 wiped out from Gold and Silver in the past 24 hours. pic.twitter.com/NwLlK9b1iv

— Whale Insider (@WhaleInsider) November 19, 2026

For traders following Bitcoin news, the obvious explanation is that money is moving out of metals and into crypto. We tested that by comparing how much money changes hands each day in the three largest US funds for silver, gold, and Bitcoin. If investors were switching, Bitcoin’s slice of that trading would grow.

Well, for now it hasn’t: Bitcoin took 30% of the money traded over the past five trading days, about the same as the 31% it took over the 20 days before.

Bitcoin’s bounce also came with less trading than the sell-off before it, a sign that buyers are still cautious.

So is this the start of a shift from metals to crypto, or just a pause in the selling?

Exchange-traded funds (ETFs) give a clean view of where US money goes, because they trade side by side on the same exchanges. We took the three biggest: the iShares Silver Trust (SLV), SPDR Gold Shares (GLD), and BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT). For each, we multiplied the closing price by the shares traded to get the dollars that changed hands each day.

So the money leaving silver and gold isn’t showing up in Bitcoin funds, at least not yet. It looks more like a broad sell-off in both, with metals now taking the heavier hit.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

Binance’s BTCUSDT pair tells the same Bitcoin news story from the crypto side. During the drop from November 13 to 15, it traded an average of $2.0 billion a day. In the three days since, as Bitcoin held above $62,000, the average fell to $1.5 billion.

Lighter trading on a bounce means fewer buyers are stepping in. Sellers have slowed down, but buyers haven’t rushed back.

Bitcoin’s spot ETFs, which hold the coin itself, show a similar picture. IBIT took in $76.5 million on November 16, its first inflow after 11 days of outflows. That’s a start, but one day of buying after two weeks of selling.

What drives both markets is the same: the US Federal Reserve. Traders expect another rate hike in December, and higher rates hurt assets that pay no interest, from silver to Bitcoin. Until that changes, a rotation from one to the other has little to feed on.

EXPLORE: Bitcoin ETF Inflows Return After Seven-Day Losing Streak as IBIT Adds $76.5M: Is the Sell-Off Finally Over?

On the daily chart, Bitcoin trades at $63,713. That is below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $75,245, and its 200-day EMA at $75,624.

The Bitcoin news to watch is volume. A move above $65,500 with trading back near $2 billion a day would be a start. If IBIT’s share of fund trading also climbs above a third, money is actually moving from metals to crypto.

As a grooming editor, I am constantly testing moisturizers, including the latest innovations and releases. I have normal to dry skin, which can also be quite sensitive and prone to acne, so I’m able to test a wide range of moisturizers for most skin types other than oily. In fact, I write a bi-monthly column detailing my favorite new releases in grooming across all categories, and moisturizers often make the cut. For this story, I collected a group of my all-time favorites, past and present, to reevaluate over the past year-plus on their ingredients, feel, consistency, and long-term effectiveness.

That being said, I am far from the only one at Men’s Health who takes skincare seriously (our office is like #boybathroom gone wild). I also considered the go-to picks of fellow editors and writers, who have been testing moisturizers since our grooming vertical first launched in 2018. I especially considered recommendations for those with oily skin, to cover all skin type bases.

Finally, I presented the extensive list of moisturizers that saw positive results to a panel of dermatologists to ensure every entry was effective and safe, while inquiring about which they recommend to their patients. With all this in mind, I narrowed our list to the ten best moisturizers for men with any skin type, be it dry, oily, sensitive, or somewhere in between.

Men need to moisturize every day—full stop. This is regardless of skin type, as even oily and acne-prone skin needs the added benefits of a moisturizing product to help regulate sebum production, according to dermatologist Dr. Corey L. Hartman, M.D. No matter your skin type, you should apply a moisturizer twice daily—once in the morning and once at night.

Moisturizer should always be the last or second-to-last step in your routine. They’re designed to not only impart hydration to your skin but also lock in the moisture that it already has, as well as the ingredients in any other products you’ve used.

An easy way to remember it is this: No matter how many products you’re using, you want to layer them from thinnest to thickest textures. After cleansing, apply any serums or other thinner products before sealing them all in with your moisturizer. In the morning, you’ll want to top the moisturizer with sunscreen, but at night, you can just end with your moisturizer.

A lot of guys skip moisturizing because they hate how it feels—greasy, heavy, or sticky formulas are instant dealbreakers. The good news? Moisturizers come in all forms, including gels, which pack high water content for fast absorption and a clean, non-tacky finish, according to dermatologist Dr. Estee Williams, M.D.

Your choice should match your skin type—gels work best for oily skin, while thicker creams suit dry patches—but the key is picking a moisturizer you actually want to use every day. If it’s just gathering dust on your shelf, it’s doing nothing for your skin.

Dermatologist Dr. Sarah Stierman, M.D., recommends using multi-tasking moisturizers that include niacinamide, which fights inflammation and prevents blemishes in oily skin; hyaluronic acid, which attracts and locks in moisture; and ceramides, which repair the skin barrier and soothe the skin, crucial for anyone who shaves regularly.

#5206. Cardano’s $5M conference budget has a $1M problem — Details!

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

The Cardano [ADA] Treasury Foundation wants 25 million ADA to host 12 events in 2027. Its last $22 million proposal (to buy copper) barely got any votes at all.

Hence, the question — Will this one fare any better?

On 16th November, the Cardano Foundation filed a proposal to pull 24,995,775 ADA from the network’s treasury. The money would pay for Cardano’s presence at 12 crypto events next year.

Some of the biggest names on the circuit are on the list. Consensus in Miami, TOKEN2049 in both Singapore and New York, Web Summit in Lisbon, and India Blockchain Week in Bangalore.

The run kicks off in February with the Africa Tech Summit in Nairobi.

$2 million will go towards sponsorships and $1.06 million for booths and equipment. Travel is said to cost $702K, while side events will account for $695,000.

According to the Foundation, none of it covers salaries or profit. Whatever isn’t spent goes back to the treasury.

However, here’s what’s tricky. The Foundation priced ADA at $0.20 to reach its $5 million budget. ADA, however, was valued at $0.15 at press time. At that price, the request is worth about $3.85 million. That is a gap of over $1 million.

For the budget to work as planned, ADA needs to climb by almost 30%. Not impossible, but far from guaranteed.

DReps, the delegates who vote on treasury spending, have until 20th December to decide.

Will 25 million ADA move the price? Probably not. There are about 37.6 billion ADA in circulation. So, this withdrawal will merely be a drop in the ocean.

However, it’s worth pointing out that the chart had bigger problems at press time.

ADA fell from $0.25 in October to $0.155 following a price drop on the 14th.

Is a pause imminent? We might be in the early stages, yes. The RSI fell to 21 after that drop, with the same since climbing to 32, just crossing above its average. The OI has also recovered from about $145 million to $153.5 million. Finally, the funding rates were positive yesterday.

On the contrary, the Chaikin Money Flow was negative, implying that sellers might still have a slight edge.

#5205. Grand Theft Crypto? GTA 6’s Fictional Coin Becomes an $18M Meme as DacityCoin Rockets 150x

GTA 6 meme coins are here: DacityCoin hit $18M as the game launched. PumpSwap volume doubled for a day, but meme coins and PUMP stay weak.

DacityCoin (DCTY) hit an $18 million market cap, the day Rockstar Games released Grand Theft Auto VI. But what is DacityCoin? Traders were racing to find GTA 6 meme coins before the game had even finished downloading.

The Solana meme is named after a fake cryptocurrency inside the game. Life imitating GTA, you could say. DCTY traded near $0.019 at 11:00 UTC, up more than 150x in 24 hours.

What the fuck? pic.twitter.com/cWJV4vGKM2

DacityCoin’s fomo doubled PumpSwap’s daily volume on Wednesday, yet the exchange was busier than it was on 12 days since October 1. Dogecoin, Pepe and Bonk barely blinked, and Pump.fun’s own token, PUMP, is sitting near a one-month low.

So is this the spark for a new run in meme coins, or just a fun one-day side quest?

EXPLORE: Bitcoin Bounces From $62K: Is Gold and Silver’s 14% Crash Sending Money Into Crypto?

DacityCoin started as a background joke. In Rockstar’s launch trailer, the name is painted on a stunt plane. Then this week, gameplay footage from Brazilian streamer Combo Infinito showed an in-game phone app listing “DacityCoin (DCTY)”, complete with buy and sell buttons.

Crypto traders did what crypto traders do: within hours, the Solana token with the same ticker went vertical.

Before the footage, DCTY had never been worth more than about $54,000. Here’s what its main pool on DEX Screener shows now:

One important detail: Rockstar hasn’t linked the in-game coin to any real token, and DCTY has no official tie to GTA 6 or Take-Two. The name game is getting messy, too.

A separate Pump.fun token called “Dacity Coin” hit a $10.8 million market value on Wednesday, then slid to about $800,000. Exchange Bitrue joined in as well, listing DacityCoin futures with up to 10x leverage on Wednesday.

If a fresh meme coin season were kicking off, Pump.fun is where you’d see it first, since that’s where most new Solana tokens of this kind are born. So we pulled PumpSwap’s daily trading from DefiLlama, which tracks exchange data across blockchains.

Outside the GTA hype, the bigger meme coins are having a rough year. All eight large meme coins we tracked on Binance are down for 2026, by a median of 54%, while Bitcoin is down 28%. The past week stung too, with drops between 11% and 23%:

Source: Binance daily closes, Coinspeaker calculation, November 19.

Zoom out, and DCTY is still tiny. The whole meme coin sector is worth $22.5 billion on CoinGecko, with Solana’s share at only $2 billion. One token can steal the spotlight for a day, but a real run for meme coins needs the big names and overall trading to rise together. So far, that hasn’t happened.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Top Solana Meme Coins to Bid

Pump.fun did get a payday out of the DacityCoin rush. The platform earned $1.62 million in revenue on Wednesday, up from a $1.28 million average over the five days before. Since April, Pump.fun says it spends half its revenue buying PUMP on the open market, so a day like Wednesday means roughly $800,000 of buying.

The worst day was November 14, when PUMP dropped 15%. Token trackers list a scheduled release of locked PUMP tokens in mid-November, though they don’t agree on the exact date. So far, buybacks of under $1 million a day haven’t been enough to soak up that selling.

GTA 6 meme coins are hot now, but the thing to watch is breadth, meaning how many coins move together. If PumpSwap volume stays above $300 million a day after launch week and Dogecoin or Pepe join in, DacityCoin could be the start of something bigger.

If DCTY fades and volume slips back to $150 million, it’ll go down as a fun launch-day story and not much more.

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

As of Nov. 20, Shiba Inu (SHIB) is about $10 million in market capitalization short of overtaking Bittensor (TAO) for the No. 33 spot in CoinMarketCap's global crypto ranking. TAO has a market cap of $2.18 billion at a price of $186.41, and SHIB has $2.17 billion at $0.000003691 and ranks No. 34.

A gain of about 0.5% in SHIB's price, with TAO's price unchanged, would be enough for the meme coin to take Bittensor's place in the ranking.

TAO is the token of the Bittensor AI network, and Digital Currency Group (DCG) founder Barry Silbert has been one of its most vocal backers. Silbert also runs Yuma, a DCG company that builds on Bittensor.

At Fortune's Brainstorm Tech conference in September 2025, Silbert said that Bittensor was the thing he had gotten most excited about since Bitcoin. "I want to open up the development and the access to AI, and Bittensor is enabling that," he said at the time. Silbert also said that Bittensor is building a "world wide web of intelligence."

On Dec. 30, 2025, DCG's Grayscale filed with the SEC to convert its Grayscale Bittensor Trust into a spot exchange-traded fund on NYSE Arca under the ticker GTAO. The filing came after Bittensor's first halving in mid-December 2025, and at the end of that month, TAO was trading at about $222. "We're pleased to take this early step as we continue to expand the tools available to investors," a Grayscale spokesperson said.

The gap between the two tokens closed because TAO fell. TAO was one of the market's strongest tokens this year. In April, the token was up 55% since January, and in October it rallied again and was up 43% for the year, according to TradingView data.

The November correction erased those gains. On Nov. 20, TAO was trading 16.95% below its January level, and it lost 12.16% over the past week.

SHIB spent most of the year in the red. The meme coin rose about 25% in January, and it has not been in positive territory since February. By Nov. 20, SHIB had lost about 50% since the start of the year, and it fell 13.79% over the past week.

TAO had a 24-hour trading volume of $172.19 million on Nov. 20, and SHIB had $55.17 million, according to CoinMarketCap data. TAO has a maximum supply of 21 million tokens, the same as Bitcoin's, and SHIB has about 589 trillion tokens in circulation.

Shiba Inu developer Mazrael responded to the drop on X on Nov. 17. "1 SHIB is always 1 SHIB," he wrote in reply to a user who pointed to the falling price.

Hong Kong has just put Hyperliquid [HYPE] on its watchlist. And yet, traders don’t seem to be bothered.

In fact, on Hyperliquid itself, the action is only heating up now.

On Wednesday, Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) added Hyperliquid to its Alert List. The problem cited was that they don’t hold a licence to operate in the city.

The regulator’s entry covers two names; Hyperliquid and Hyperliquid Hong Kong. It also shared the exchange’s trading website. It is believed that the platform may be serving Hong Kong users, presenting itself as a local operator, or pitching its services to people in the city.

With this addition, the SFC’s list of suspicious crypto trading platforms has grown to 69 names now. At the time of writing, Hyperliquid hadn’t commented on the development.

Back in June, Singapore’s central bank placed Hyperliquid on its Investor Alert List which flags firms people might wrongly assume are regulated there. At the time, Hyperliquid’s response was simple — it never said it had a Singapore licence.

Now, there are two Asian financial hubs keeping an eye on the exchange.

While Hong Kong was flagging Hyperliquid, traders on the platform were busy betting on Anthropic.

On 18th November, the number of traders holding long positions on Anthropic perps hit a record 5,567.

A week ago, that figure was 2,926; nearly doubling in seven days. There were 1,996 short holders, with the same hinting at 2.8 longs for every short.

Most of that action was on Trade[XYZ]’s ANT market. According to Token Terminal, this alone accounted for 4,190 long holders,.

One caveat, though. These numbers count traders, not the size of their bets. And since the data adds up three markets, anyone trading on two of them gets counted twice.

The altcoin was trading at $67.66, at press time, following a hike of just 1% in the last 24 hours. Its price was still a long way from its late-October levels when it briefly climbed above $95. Since then, it’s been mostly downhill for the crypto.

There seemed to be some sign of a breather though. The RSI was below 30 during that drop. It has since come back to just nudging above its average.

The CMF at -0.06 suggested that sellers still had the upper hand, but the outflows were clearly weaker than earlier this month.

#5202. The Best Men's Travel Blazers in 2026, Tested by Style Editors

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

Silhouettes from Uniqlo, Suitsupply, and Eddie Bauer went the distance in our testing.

WHETHER YOU’RE PACKING for a trip or just gearing up for a long commute, keeping a travel blazer in your rotation saves you time—and a lot of outfit stress. When you’re bouncing from one to the next with no time to reset, this is the one piece in your wardrobe that won’t fall apart. Unlike traditional blazers, these travel styles resist wrinkles, breathe easily, and have enough stretch that you still feel comfortable during those cramped flights and shoulder-to-shoulder train rides. On top of that, they’re easy to pack in your luggage and pair with a bunch of ensembles.

Since 2022, we’ve tested over 25 travel blazers, seeing how they hold up in overhead bins, on sweaty commutes, and straight out of a bag. The best ones are tailored, not restrictive, lightweight but not flimsy, and polished without feeling overdone. No one’s traveling in a three-piece suit anymore. Here are the best travel blazers to get you through it all.

In the past year, our style team has tested dozens of travel blazers for functionality and Relwen has it in spades. Right off the bat, we noticed that its cotton-spandex fabric feels super lightweight and comes with enough stretch to let you move beyond limitations. It leans more sport jacket with a four-button design and throat latch that allows you to button all the way up to your neck. There are also functional buttons on the sleeves, which look sharp rolled up. I’ve worn it in low 50s as well as high 70s, and found it to be comfortable in both temps.

Normally, I have to pay to dry clean most of my blazers, but this one can be tossed around my washing machine without falling apart. As for storage, the three exterior patch pockets are similar to any casual blazer, but the large interior pocket has a zip closure with a vertical opening for easy access. It is ideal for stashing valuables.

On top of being a solid choice for away seminars or long flights, this option is great for everyday wear. It looks great during cool evening strolls, dinner dates, and outdoor weddings. Sure, this blazer gets wrinkled easily, but it’s designed to give off a laid-back vibe, as if it’s been worn and broken in over time.

In Rhone’s vast assortment, the brand carries a travel blazer with a killer slim cut. It has a sporty vibe, but looks clean enough for meetings that aren’t too formal. The Flex-Knit fabric is breathable and moisture-wicking, which means you stay cool and the garment doesn’t become damp or develop unpleasant odors from sweat. The polyester material has plenty of stretch, so I never felt any restriction in the arm area when I grabbed my coffee or reached up to the high cabinet.

I’ve paired it with everything from a basic tee to an oxford shirt, and it looks great with just about anything in your wardrobe—a true testament to its versatility. Plus, the material is ultra-light, making it a comfortable pick to throw on. Unlike Relwen’s travel blazer, this one can’t go in the washer—you have to take a trip to the dry cleaners.

Eddie Bauer’s travel blazer is practically indestructible. The fabric is hardcore and can take a beating, thanks to the reinforced seams and durable water-repellent finish. The latter especially makes sure you’re covered if you spill a drink or get caught in a downpour. And when you’re commuting, you can secure your passport or phone inside zippered compartments.

During our testing, we found that the two-way stretch made a journey a breeze, giving us the freedom to move through busy airports and crowded streets. Plus, the universal fit hits the sweet spot, so it’s comfortable for all body types without being too tight or too loose.

Although Uniqlo’s design looks like a wool blazer replica, it’s one of the most breathable styles I’ve ever worn. It’s made with the brand’s proprietary AirSense fabric, a lightweight polyester material that dries in minutes and keeps me cool. Typically, when I wear a traditional blazer in the summertime and in the muggy subway, I sweat like a dog. But when I wore this one in 80-degree weather to a work brunch, I was comfortable and dry the whole time. It’s relaxed enough to wear with chinos or jeans, but still has a dressy vibe that can pull off a full-suit look with trousers.

I found it’s not too fitted in the waist, which lets me layer shirts or knits easier in the cooler temps. There’s no bunching to where I feel stuffed. You can snag it in the typical neutral colors like gray and navy, perfect for the office followed by dinner plans. Like Relwen’s offering, this one is machine washable, but I recommend turning it inside out in a mesh bag. On the other hand, it’s way more structured with a natural shaping in the shoulders and sleeves. And yeah, it’s the most affordable option on this list, clocking in under $100, but it doesn’t look or feel like a budget buy. You’re getting the same premium quality that you’d get with a blazer that cost a few hundred bucks.

In an effort to max out comfort, Faherty offers a travel blazer made out of a stretch jersey knit fabric. It has a soft hand feel, tailored fit, and wears like your coziest cardigan. The front pockets are deep enough to carry your earbuds or wallet, so either won’t fall out as you’re maneuvering through the airport. Whether you’re packing it all in a backpack or suitcase, it’s a breeze to toss in and hit the road. Plus, we found no signs of wrinkles after unloading our clothes in the hotel.

Unlike stiff travel blazers that we’ve tested, this one bends and moves with you, so it doesn’t feel like you’re stuck in a straightjacket. The slimmer cut is perfect for guys who have an athletic or lean build, as it accentuates a trim silhouette and creates a sharp appearance. It’s a perfect match with a pair of summer pants, but looks just as cool with jeans and a tee.

When you want to look like you mean business at client dinners or conferences, you should reach for this blazer from Hugo Boss. Most travel blazers prioritize comfort at the expense of polish, but this one manages to deliver both. Our Style and Reviews Director Christian Gollayan loves how sharp this slim-fit silhouette looks on him. He says it's tailored without feeling restrictive, while the stretch-infused, polyester-wool fabric gives you enough mobility for long flights and days spent hauling luggage through airports. The biggest differentiator, though, is right in the name: it’s washable. I can wear it repeatedly on a multi-day trip, freshen it up without a costly dry-cleaning bill, and pack it with far less anxiety than a traditional wool sport coat.

I wore the jacket on a full travel day that included a flight, a lengthy commute, and several hours seated at meetings. It kept its shape surprisingly well, resisting the creases and rumpling that typically throw off more formal tailoring after being folded inside a carry-on. What impressed me most was how effortlessly it transitioned from travel wear to evening attire. I could step off a plane and head directly to a dinner reservation without feeling underdressed. Admittedly, the jacket isn’t as soft or unstructured as more casual travel blazers from performance-focused brands. Also, the slimmer cut may feel less forgiving if you prefer a relaxed fit. But if your priority is maintaining a clean, business-ready vibe while still getting travel-friendly performance, I haven’t found many options that strike the balance as well as this one.

If you’re looking for a travel blazer that leans more dressy with European tailoring and luxurious quality for a great price point, Suitsupply is your best bet. Instead of a boxy, rigid silhouette that’s on trend right now, this timeless design has a natural shoulder, single-breasted closure, and a half-canvas construction that helps the jacket mold to your body over time while maintaining a solid drape.

It’s made with medium weight pure wool, but I wasn’t burning up wearing it with a tank top at a rooftop party. When the temperature really spikes beyond 80 degrees, I would recommend reaching for something lighter like linen. The chest and waist is trimmed for a slim fit, but it’s not too tight in the arms. I wore a 36R and didn’t need any alteration. It looks sharp straight off the rack. Sure, it’s on the pricier end compared to other picks on the list, but you’ll have this blazer for seasons to come. You can wear it to the office, formal business events, or weddings.

Linen blazers, like this one by Charles Tyrwhitt, reign supreme for travel because I stay cool, dry, and comfortable. Even though this design’s fabric blends cotton and linen, you’re still getting a hefty dose of linen (53%), so it wears as light as a feather. As I’m commuting, airflow is constant, and it never feels stuffy like wool, even when the temps spike. Linen is notorious for wrinkling, but this one’s got enough structure that creases barely register—and the taupe color blends in, helping to mask any wrinkles that do show up.

The cut is relaxed through the chest and waist, with a clean, structured drape that follows the body without pulling. The shoulders are lightly structured, giving you shape up top without feeling stiff. It’s a sharper silhouette overall, but still works for guys with broader shoulders or a bigger chest. But if you’re on the leaner side, it captures that close-to-the-body, tailored look.

If you want a blazer that feels like a step up from your usual travel uniform, I would highly consider this number from Bonobos. Unlike stiff, restrictive blazers that make you feel like you’re trapped in a straightjacket, this cotton-spandex blend flexes with you, whether you’re reaching for your luggage in the overhead bin or hailing a cab. I have to admit, it does wrinkle quite a bit when I’m sitting down for a long amount of time. In true Bonobos fashion, this blazer comes in three fits—slim, athletic, and standard—so every guy can find his perfect match. And it’s far more relaxed than a traditional sport coat. Just a note: you can only take it to the dry cleaners. In terms of styling, it’s super versatile: you can wear it with a dress shirt and chinos for a garden party or a casual T-shirt and jeans for a laid-back look on your next trip.

Read more: Bonobos Jetsetter Blazer Review

If I’m traveling somewhere warm and still want to look put-together, Buck Mason’s carry-on blazer is the one I keep coming back to. Its cotton-linen blend combines the breathability of pure linen along with the durability and structure of cotton. You get that relaxed, cool texture that makes linen so comfortable in the summer, but without the excessive wrinkling that can make traditional linen jackets look disheveled halfway through a trip.

What I liked most was how well it handled repeated packing and unpacking. While it picked up some natural creasing—as any linen-rich garment will—it never looked sloppy. The cotton component helped the jacket retain its shape, while the linen kept it noticeably cooler than traditional wool tailoring during warm afternoons. At 5’8”, I also appreciated that the silhouette felt tailored without being overly structured or stiff. The jacket’s biggest strength is versatility. It pairs just as naturally with chinos and loafers for a dinner reservation as it does with shorts and minimal sneakers for a day of sightseeing.

Unlike performance travel blazers that can sometimes look overly technical, the Capitola leans into classic menswear styling with a fabric that develops character the more you wear it. It’s not the blazer I’d choose for highly formal business settings, but for warm-weather travel, it’s one of the most wearable options I’ve tested.

When shopping for men’s travel blazers, look for fabrics that are comfy and practical. Men’s travel blazers are built to look like traditional blazers, while providing the feel and function of athletic outerwear. Go for stretchy materials like spandex or elastane, so you can move without any hassle or restriction. Wrinkle-resistant materials like polyester or blends are great because they remain looking sharp after you unravel them from your suitcase. Breathable materials like cotton and lightweight wool keep you cool and comfortable.

Make sure your blazer fits well and is comfortable enough to wear all day. Travel blazers for men should allow freedom of movement and not feel too tight or restrictive. The shoulders of the garment need to align with your own and not sag or pinch, as this affects the overall look. Always double-check the sleeves; see that they’re not too long and the armholes are high enough to avoid bunching while allowing mobility. When it comes to travel blazers, you'll typically find these three main types of fits.

A more tailored cut that's snug around the chest and waist, giving you a sharp, sleek silhouette. Great for guys who want a more fitted look without sacrificing comfort.

A fit that's perfect for guys with broader shoulders and a smaller waist. It offers more room in the chest and shoulders, while still tapering at the waist for a streamlined look.

The classic, relaxed fit. It offers more room throughout the body and is great for a laid-back, comfortable look. Ideal for guys who prioritize freedom of movement and a less structured feel.

A packable travel blazer can easily be folded or rolled up if it's taking too much space in your luggage, leaving room for other essentials. Having one that packs well means you can just throw it in the bag and go, making your travel preparations simpler and more efficient.

Check for practical features like multiple pockets for easy access to essentials and moisture-wicking properties if you intend to be active.

To find the best travel blazers for men, our style team led by Style and Reviews Director Christian Gollayan, tested dozens over the past few years. We wore them during business conferences, day trips, and leisure vacations. We tested each one, checking to see which allowed for easy movement, felt light, and fit nicely throughout the body. We also analyzed the packing process and styled the blazer with different outfits to make sure it worked for both casual and formal settings. We then narrowed down to the eight best travel blazers for men that give you a stylish and refined look that attracts only the best kind of attention.

Think of your travel blazer more like a lightweight jacket. Any blazer in a dark, neutral color or simple pattern can go on top of pretty much any outfit. Whether you wear a button-down shirt or a hoodie, throwing a blazer over it instantly levels up your look. Alas, we tend to not use the pockets of suits or formal blazers very often, but you should utilize all the pocket space of travel blazers.

Anthropic’s post-IPO performance appears to have created a volatile market setup.

On the technical side, ANT opened at $111.50, around 34% above its $83 IPO price, before losing much of its early gains and closing at $97.17. This shows that initial demand was strong, but profit-taking quickly kicked in. The impact also seems to have spilled over into crypto, with the total market cap forming its third consecutive lower low at $2.08 trillion, a level last seen in early Q3.

Naturally, this raises a question: Is crypto’s weakness simply a result of ANT-driven volatility? Interestingly, recent Glassnode data points to a possible link. As the chart below shows, Anthropic futures on crypto platforms recorded $9.5 billion in trading volume ahead of its Nasdaq debut. In comparison, SpaceX, the largest IPO on record, attracted $3.9 billion in pre-listing futures volume before its June debut.

In essence, ANT’s pre-IPO futures generated more than 2.4x SpaceX’s.

This highlights how much larger speculative interest in ANT was compared to SpaceX, setting a new record for pre-IPO trading activity on crypto platforms. However, the initial hype quickly turned into profit-taking, with ANT dropping 13% from its opening price. This shift in sentiment may have added to Bitcoin’s [BTC] selling pressure, especially as liquidation activity picked up alongside the broader market breakdown.

So, is Bitcoin’s latest breakdown the start of an overall deleveraging process in crypto markets? In other words, could IPO-driven volatility have accelerated long liquidations, forced overleveraged traders out of positions, and triggered a general market reset?

It looks like ANT’s futures activity on crypto platforms may have added to the selling pressure.

According to CoinGlass, over $700 million worth of positions have been liquidated in the last 24 hours. Of that amount, nearly $600 million was long positions, indicating that leveraged bulls have been badly hit by the correction. However, can this flush-out in Futures markets lead to a rebalance?

Worth mentioning here is the ongoing liquidity drain. In the last 30 days, $11.5 billion has left the stablecoin supply. That outflow is greater than it was in the aftermath of the Terra collapse in 2022. While many in the crypto market are looking at Bitcoin’s price movements, the real problem is the decreasing capital in crypto.

Why does this matter? Lower stablecoin supply means less available liquidity to support buying activity, which could keep pressure on Bitcoin and the broader market.

So, while ANT-related volatility may have contributed to market deleveraging, liquidity is still very poor for a sustained recovery. In this context, ANT’s IPO may have added to an already fragile market, while concerns around its valuation may also “continue” to create a risk-off sentiment in U.S. markets.

Against this backdrop, a drop in the total crypto market cap below $2 trillion cannot be ruled out.

ANT’s IPO may have added to Bitcoin’s fear and increased crypto selling.

Weak liquidity could keep pressure on crypto, putting the $2 trillion market cap at risk.

Cotton may be the most dependable fabric for regular every-day t-shirts, but cotton holds onto moisture, which makes it a sweat trap, weighing you down. Instead, opt for synthetic, moisture-wicking fabrics like polyester and nylon that are lighter. They can also be woven in special ways that cotton can't be to enhance breathability. Synthetic fibers don't bleed and are hard to discolor, so they won't get sweat stains. Some menswear brands are even starting to use finely knit wool for its natural breathability, moisture wicking, and odor-fighting properties. Consider what feels best to you and in what environment you might be working out in.

In most clothing, seams are placed where they are easiest to construct the shirt or look the best. However, those places—like under your armpit and along the side of your body—are also high friction areas, especially when working out. Athletic brands have designed t-shirts that minimize the amount of seams and place them in areas that wont be impacted by your movement. Look out for seams and other high-contact areas that could prose a problem, depending on where they're located.

Simply put, your workout clothes get stinky when they hold on to sweat. A whole range of innovations exist that brands claim will fight odor, but the only sure fire way to keep your workout shirts from stinking are to keep them dry and wash them after every use. That means the workout shirts that retain the least amount of sweat are the easiest to keep from stinking. So if odor is a concern for you (as it should be), look for the shirts that dry the fastest and breath the best. There's a lot of new tech out now that helps combat stink.

Forward thinking labels are adding UV protection to workout clothes. Sunscreen is great, but even the best sweat-proof kinds can wear off during long and intense outdoor exercises. Not so with UPF clothing, which block UV rays to keep you protected during your entire sweat session, no reapplication necessary. Even the Skin Cancer Foundation has touted the skin-saving benefits of UPF clothing. If you're looking for even more sun protection, look for long-sleeve t-shirts, or hooded tops with UPF features.

Synthetic fabrics work especially well in workout shirts, as they're designed to handle moisture better than traditional materials. These fabrics include: polyester, Gore-Tex, nylon, and spandex, which have tiny spaces in knit or mesh that allow moisture to move through, evaporating quickly.

According to Dr. Corey L. Hartman, MD, an assistant clinical professor of dermatology at the University of Alabama School of Medicine, moisture-wicking fabrics help moisture from the inner layer of the fabric (the part that touches your skin) escape to the outside of the garment.

"Synthetic materials are better at moisture-wicking as they not only pull sweat moisture away from the skin, but they also dry quickly and don’t hold onto moisture," explains. Dr. Marisa Garshick, board-certified dermatologist of MDCS Dermatology.

"Cotton, on the other hand, while it can absorb sweat and moisture from the skin, it is more likely to hold onto the moisture and not dry as quickly, leaving the sweat in prolonged contact with the skin," she explains. Although, some cotton fabrics may be specially treated to make them moisture wicking.

Double checking the tags on your tops, or reading about the materials it's made of will help you pick proper shirts for your workouts. And thankfully, you can find moisture-wicking materials in tanks, short sleeve tees, long sleeve tees and hoodies.

So, why buy a workout shirt anyway? We've all worked out out in a regular cotton t-shirt at one time or another, and while it certainly won't ruin your gym session, it won't make it more enjoyable either.

The result of wearing shirts designed for athletic performance is that the fabric from which they're made feels drier and cooler against the skin.

"Moisture-wicking [shirts] can be especially beneficial when the body is subject to higher temperatures, like during a workout or a hot summer day," Dr. Hartman explains. Plus, keeping things cool and dry under your shirt can actually minimize a slew of issues.

"Buildup of sweat can lead to irritation which can appear as red, flaky patches or breakouts, which appear as red papules or pustules that may involve the hair follicle," explains Dr. Garshick.

There are some body odor perks, too (or lack thereof), according to Dr. Hartman. "Body odor occurs when sweat mixes with natural bacteria found on the skin. The less sweat on the skin, the less body odor."

#5197. XRP Faces Severe Supply Shortage on Binance

The price of XRP has continued to slump to deeper levels amid the prolonged market volatility. However, recent onchain data has shown an unexpected trend in exchange activity.

According to the latest data from crypto analytics platform Cryptoquant, XRP is currently facing a severe supply shortage on the world’s largest crypto exchange, Binance.

According to the data, XRP’s Supply Shortage Index on Binance has surged to 2.4 as of November 19 despite the asset’s extreme price weakness in recent days.

Notably, the data further shows that the metric has surpassed the previous reading of 2.09 recorded on July 6, marking a five-month high in XRP’s supply shortage index.

It is important to note that readings above +2 are a strong indication of severely tightened supply, which means that the amount of XRP available on the exchange has decreased significantly.

While negative readings often mean the opposite, this means that XRP has witnessed a sharp reversal from the supply level seen on September 27.

At the time, the index stood at -1.5 while XRP traded above $1.50, signaling an abundance of XRP on Binance. This means that more tokens were available for trading during the period, which potentially added to selling pressure.

While that is no longer the case, the latest data shows that the XRP supply index has jumped by 3.9 points in just 53 days, moving from supply abundance to severe supply tightness in just about two months.

This typically suggests that XRP is being aggressively moved out of exchanges despite its prolonged price weakness, potentially driving a rebound in the demand for XRP, which could eventually trigger a price recovery.

#5195. Bitcoin Shows Unprecedented Weakness, Price Hits 4.5-Month Low

Bitcoin (BTC), the world’s largest cryptocurrency, is flashing a major, ‘scary’ technical signal that was absent even during its last major crashes in February and June 2026.

The flagship coin has crashed to a fresh 4.5-month low amid persistent institutional outflows totaling billions from cryptocurrency exchange-traded funds (ETFs).

$BTC hasn't formed a higher high for 16 consecutive days now. This didn't even happen during the Feb 2026 and June 2026 crashes. https://t.co/I6IPmdueEc

Bitcoin has failed to form a higher high for the past 16 days. This is a very long stretch, one that was absent during Bitcoin’s February and June crashes.

A higher high, in the context of technical analysis, is formed when an asset’s price reaches a new high point above its previous swing high. The absence of higher highs signals that buyers are having a hard time taking back control of the market.

The latest Bitcoin price action adds further to concerns surrounding the future of the flagship cryptocurrency.

Earlier today, BTC crashed to $61,225, its lowest price point in around four and a half months.

Bitcoin's failure to create higher highs despite several attempts to recover shows that selling pressure remains quite high.

Nevertheless, this technical pattern of 16 days without a higher high does not necessarily spell more pain for Bitcoin. If the cryptocurrency can decisively push above recent resistance zones, it may be a sign that buyers are starting to make a comeback.

Bitcoin is facing persistent withdrawals of huge amounts of money from U.S.-based spot Bitcoin ETFs.

BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) witnessed its biggest-ever daily net outflow on Nov. 19.

The crypto fund suffered a whopping $541.1 million in net withdrawals on the day. At the same time, total net outflows from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs amounted to around $582.3 million across the entire market.

More alarmingly, the fresh wave of withdrawals brings cumulative net outflows from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs to around $3.47 billion so far this November.

The ETFs have seen negative net flows on 12 of the first 14 trading days of the month.
